Code shape as claimed: `products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:222` does `from products.stamphog.backend.facade.api import queue_inbox_pr_review` outside the `try` at 224-234, and the callback is registered with plain `transaction.on_commit(...)` (line 131, no `robust=True`). Django 5.2.17 (`.flox/cache/venv/.../django/db/backends/base/base.py:727-766`): a non-robust callback's exception propagates, either immediately in autocommit or from the outermost `atomic()` exit after commit.

Callers traced. Writers of `TaskRun.output`: (1) `set_task_run_output` at `products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:2154` saves in autocommit, so the callback runs inline inside the receiver's outer `try/except` at `receivers.py:81-141`; (2) the webhook writer `_record_run_output_field` at `products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:284-297` wraps its `atomic()` in a `try`; (3) the PATCH writer `update_task_run` at `products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:2027-2072` runs the save inside `with transaction.atomic():` with NO enclosing try, and the DRF view `partial_update` at `products/tasks/backend/presentation/views/api.py:1082-1090` adds none. So the validator's refutation is incomplete: on the PATCH path, an exception from the callback WOULD escape as a 500 after the row committed.

However the only exception the finding names is an ImportError from line 222, and that has no reachable trigger. `products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:9-13` imports only `..models`, `.contracts`, `.enums`; `products/stamphog/backend/models.py:10-18` imports django, `posthog.models.scoping.product_mixin`, `posthog.models.utils`, and `.facade.enums`. All are unconditional, in-repo, always-installed modules with no optional dependency or settings gate. By request time every module is fully loaded, so no partial-module circular import can occur; the deferral exists only for startup weight (comment at 219-221). The identical deferred-import-outside-try shape is preexisting in `_start_review` at `receivers.py:254-255`. The `queue_inbox_pr_review` body (broker publish, the thing that can actually fail) is inside the `try` at 225-231, matching the docstring's promise at line 213.
votes.refutation: The import at line 222 can only raise if the deployed build is broken (module missing or a top-level import error in stamphog's facade/models), which is a CI-caught, deploy-blocking condition rather than a runtime edge case; every real failure mode of the dispatch (broker down, bad args) is already inside the try. So the claimed "error after the transaction committed" has no reachable trigger in a healthy build, and it is the same shape the module already uses at lines 254-255. Not a real defect. If hardening is wanted anyway, the cheap fix is `transaction.on_commit(..., robust=True)` at lines 116 and 131 (or moving the import inside the try), which would also cover the PATCH writer path the validator missed.

votes.refutation: Attempted refutation: the finding needs (a) a writer that saves TaskRun.output inside an outer transaction with no error guard, and (b) the deferred import raising at runtime. (a) exists via the PATCH path (`update_task_run`), so the validator's stated reason for rejection is wrong on that point. (b) fails: the imported module has no cycle with review_hog, its app is installed in production config, it is imported on other production paths and in tests, and an ImportError would be deterministic across every process rather than a request-time failure.
